classification.difficultyReason: Translate each reciprocal equation into a two-branch sketch using its sign and axis asymptotes, then choose and evaluate a convenient nonzero x-value to label a point.

content.prompt: Sketch the following hyperbolas. Make sure to label a unique point on your graph.

answer.short: Branches in quadrants I and III; labelled point $(1,1)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{1}{1}\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
Plot $(1,1)$. Draw two smooth branches in quadrants I and III, approaching the asymptotes $x=0$ and $y=0$.

spec.description: Complete reciprocal sketch with two arrowed branches and a labelled point; no grid or numeric axis ticks.
spec.mathematics: y=1/x; point (1,1); asymptotes x=0 and y=0.

answer.short: Branches in quadrants I and III; labelled point $(2,2)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{4}{2}\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Plot $(2,2)$. Draw two smooth branches in quadrants I and III, approaching the asymptotes $x=0$ and $y=0$.

spec.description: Complete reciprocal sketch with branches in quadrants I and III and point label above the positive branch.
spec.mathematics: y=4/x; point (2,2); asymptotes x=0 and y=0.

answer.short: Branches in quadrants II and IV; labelled point $(-1,2)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac{2}{-1}\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Plot $(-1,2)$. Draw two smooth branches in quadrants II and IV, approaching the asymptotes $x=0$ and $y=0$.

spec.description: Negative reciprocal graph with the labelled point placed above and left, away from the curve.
spec.mathematics: y=-2/x; point (-1,2); asymptotes x=0 and y=0.

answer.short: Branches in quadrants II and IV; labelled point $\left(\dfrac12,-1\right)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac{1}{2\left(\frac12\right)}\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
Plot $\left(\dfrac12,-1\right)$. Draw two smooth branches in quadrants II and IV, approaching the asymptotes $x=0$ and $y=0$.

spec.description: Negative reciprocal graph with a complete fractional coordinate label below and right of its point.
spec.mathematics: y=-1/(2x); point (1/2,-1); asymptotes x=0 and y=0.
